features.title: Mermaid diagrams in the conversation
features.summary: A ```mermaid fence renders as a themed diagram card wherever Chat's code-fence registry applies: assistant answers, reasoning, compaction summaries, ask_user_question text and backlog item text. A fence becomes a diagram once it is complete (another block follows it, or the message settles); until then the native code card stays. The card keeps the code's height while pele loads and fades the diagram in; its header toggles between the diagram and its highlighted source and copies the source; clicking the diagram expands it full size. pele (Obsidian's Mermaid renderer, MIT) draws the SVG through DOMPurify with links, images, styles and foreignObject removed; $$…$$ labels are typeset with KaTeX MathML, loaded only for such a diagram, under a profile that admits only KaTeX's MathML inside foreignObject. Colors come from the DSH theme, so light and dark switch without re-rendering. Neither renderer is in client.js: the Host serves pele's ES module build and katex.mjs from /dshfiles-mermaid-diagrams/renderer/ through dshx StaticAssets, and the Client imports them on first use.
failureModes: Source pele cannot parse shows the parse error above the highlighted source, with the recovery to fix the source or ask the agent to correct it.

The renderer cannot be downloaded (no web server route, a dropped connection, a diagram type's parser that fails to load): the card names the cause and offers Retry, which imports the module again under a new URL; the source stays readable through Show code.
dist/renderer holds a pele without mountAsync: the card says the renderer is out of date and to rebuild the plugin, then reload.
KaTeX cannot be loaded: math labels stay readable TeX.
The renderer route meets a file-system fault other than a missing file: it answers 500 with the fault on the span instead of a 404.
A renderer exception falls back to the native code card (Chat's code-fence boundary).
